answer.why: As an insider I laugh at it straight away, because 'confirmed and substantive' is the exact phrase from the appointment letter, the moment you stop being on probation or acting. Only someone who has actually been through the service would pick that title, so I would trust the details to be right. 'Minister Salary' is the cheaper hook, since every Singaporean has an opinion on it, but it reads like a meme or a political rant and I would worry the game is just a dig at the system.
answer.expect_minister_salary: A satirical, slightly clickbaity game about the million-dollar ministerial pay debate, where the goal is probably to get rich or reach the top. I would expect it to be shallow and a bit preachy, with a punchline in place of an accurate picture of how the service works. It would appeal to outsiders more than to me.
answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: A dry, wry, insider-flavoured career sim about the slow grind of promotion, appraisals and acting appointments. I would expect it to get the details right, with the meeting about the meeting and the careful wording of performance reviews, and to be quietly funny rather than loud. It might be a niche title that outsiders would not understand, but I would be happy to be its audience.

agent.why: Quiet years are when you fix the plumbing nobody sees, and it worked for me back in Y17.
agent.confused_by: The header says $40.38M but the package is about $2.5M; still unexplained.
agent.note: Nice line about Bintan being either a compliment or a warning, very insider.
agent.remember: Y35: DPM MR1 MHA, quiet year. Chose A, fixed something unasked as in Y17. STAND 81 (-2), still sliding; see whether a non-walkabout action moves it.

best_moment.what: Listening to the chilli stallholder on camera and watching STAND recover. It was the one time a small human choice visibly paid off, and it felt true to how a walkabout actually works.

worst_moment.what: The fourth walkabout with the chilli stallholder. By then the repeat was tedious, and STAND kept sliding whatever I chose, so the choice felt decorative.

skip_year.why: Same walkabout and same stallholder as the years either side, with no new information and a small STAND drop. It could have been folded into one beat.

answer.held_back_by: Nothing really did. I reached PM with REP, INTEG and COMP at 100. If anything held me back, it was STAND sliding from my honesty, but it never blocked the climb. I suspect it was only a decoration stat.
answer.ending_fair_why: A cautious, honest, competent officer reaching the top feels plausible, and the card's line that the formula was published is a sharp, accurate jab. But the run felt too smooth, since nothing I did ever truly blocked me.
answer.chase_next: I would chase an early exit to the private sector or a failed bid. I want to see whether the game punishes ambition, tea invitations declined, or a bad appraisal, because I never saw any real failure state.
answer.play_again_why: The institutional details were good, but the late years repeated events and my choices did not seem to change the outcome. I would wait a while, or try it only to see a failure path.

tone_breaks.line: Pay header in $M versus a package of about $2.5M
tone_breaks.note: The pay figures were inconsistent and never explained. For a game about salary formulas, that undermines the premise.

tone_breaks.line: The formula pays you twice the entry-grade minister's salary
tone_breaks.note: Not how the benchmark works, as I understand it. The PM's salary is set as a multiple of a benchmark, not of the entry-grade minister's pay. Also, the PM's pay is not a feature of the formula applied to the entry grade.

answer.title_fit_why: The game is really about the pay package each year, and the ending card ends on earnings and the formula. The Confirmed & Substantive angle, about appraisals and grades, was only lightly touched.
